cards.title: Running out on Sunday night is avoidable
cards.body: Most medicine gaps aren't about forgetting. The strip simply ran out before anyone noticed. Refill reminders fix that.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: From the dose and the quantity given, you can tell roughly when a strip will finish. A reminder comes a few days before.

cards.title: For patients: no gaps
cards.body: Long-term BP and sugar medicines need regular use. A timely refill means no missed days waiting for the shop to open.

cards.title: For chemists: stock ready
cards.body: Knowing who needs what, and when, means fewer "kal aana" moments and less last-minute ordering.

cards.title: For families: less tracking
cards.body: Nobody has to count tablets over a video call. The reminder does the remembering.

cards.title: A refill isn't a renewal
cards.body: If a prescription has ended or is due for review, the reminder is a cue to see the doctor, not just to buy more.

cards.title: Small nudge, steady care
cards.body: Reminders keep routine medicines routine. AICA is building refill predictions for pharmacies, with pilots starting in Lucknow.

takeaway: Refill reminders prevent gaps for patients, help chemists stock up, and flag when it's time to see the doctor again.
share: Send this to the chemist who still keeps a refill diary by hand.
